items: Ginger beef was invented at Calgary's Silver Inn Restaurant in the 1970s.
On January 11, 1911, Fort Vermilion recorded a temperature of about -61°C, the coldest recorded in Alberta.
In 1884, geologist Joseph Burr Tyrrell discovered a dinosaur skull near present-day Drumheller that was later named Albertosaurus.
The name Albertosaurus means 'lizard from Alberta'.
The Royal Tyrrell Museum near Drumheller houses one of the world's largest displays of dinosaur remains.
Banff National Park is Canada's first national park.
Wood Buffalo National Park stretches across Alberta and the Northwest Territories and is Canada's largest national park.
The enormous Big Rock near Okotoks was carried out of the Rocky Mountains by glacial ice.
Head-Smashed-In Buffalo Jump preserves more than 6,000 years of Plains buffalo culture.
Alberta's rat-control program has worked since 1950 to prevent rats from establishing a permanent population.
The world's largest beaver dam is in Alberta's Wood Buffalo National Park and stretches almost 800 metres.
